new_observations: Backend selection: the default is 'python' everywhere: CameraBackendManager.backend='python', the CameraGroupCreateRequest.backend default, and the UI store. 'rust' is chosen per camera group through the API 'backend' field or a 'Camera backend' dropdown in the UI sidebar. Switching backends requires closing all cameras first. Evidence: upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/camera_group/camera_backend_manager.py:26,30,35-40; upstream/sfn26:skellycam/api/http/cameras/camera_router.py:25,127; upstream/sfn26:skellycam-ui/src/store/slices/cameras/cameras-slice.ts:31; upstream/sfn26:skellycam-ui/src/components/camera-config-tree-view/CameraConfigSidebarPanel.tsx:58-65 (commit 6cb170f2).

The record endpoints changed from GET to POST: /group/all/record/stop is now POST, and pause_unpause became PUT /group/all/pause with a body. Clients that call stop with GET, as the review's harness and possibly FreeMoCap did, would get 405 on sfn26. Evidence: upstream/sfn26:skellycam/api/http/cameras/camera_router.py:140,163,214-218; commit f1aefa95 (2026-11-01).

Finalization is stricter and more all-or-nothing. save_to_file now runs VideoAssociations.resolve_paths(strict=True), which raises if any camera's video file is missing. save_to_file is the first step of finalize_recording, so one missing video now aborts the whole finalize: no info JSON, no CSVs, no stats. Before, the info JSON and CSVs were written first and only validate_recording failed. Evidence: upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/recorders/videos/video_associations.py:36-48; upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/recorders/videos/recording_info.py:86-90; upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/recorders/recording_finalizer.py:55.

Playback now depends on the info JSON. Per-camera timing and the video-to-camera mapping are read from the new 'videos' and 'camera_timing' fields of every *_info.json in the folder, and conflicting values raise. Pre-sfn26 recordings lack those fields, so playback falls back to frame/fps timing. That fallback uses the biased header fps, so playback timestamps for old recordings carry the ~9-10% error (inferred). Evidence: upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/recorders/videos/recording_metadata.py:14-29; upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/timestamps/recording_timing_reader.py:18-31; upstream/sfn26:skellycam/api/http/playback/playback_router.py:303-311.

Per-camera CSV naming is fixed to match camera IDs: process_and_save_recording_timestamps now checks that the metadata and config key sets are equal and reorders the metadata by config key before creating the CSVs. This touches R6 and fixes the CSV-name mismatch inside the finalizer. Evidence: upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/timestamps/numpy_timestamps/process_and_save_recording_timestamps.py:32-36,84-87; commit dc578551 (2026-11-01).

Rust path: the 27-column per-camera CSV has the same headers but different meanings. pre_frame_grab=loop_start, post_frame_grab=frame_available, post_retrieve=post_jpeg_extract, and the shm columns hold pre_send/gatherer_received. So the 'main timestamp' (grab midpoint) and the lifecycle durations are not comparable with Python-backend recordings. Evidence: upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/camera_group/rust_recording.py:32-44; upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/timestamps/numpy_timestamps/create_camera_csvs.py:50-51.

Rust path: native timestamps are streamed to CSV and flushed after every row during the recording, so they survive a crash, unlike the Python path. The Python-format CSVs, info JSON and stats are still written only after a clean stop. Evidence: upstream/sfn26:skellycam-rust/src/timestamps/csv_writer.rs:50-73; upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/camera_group/rust_camera_group.py:137-155.

Rust path, latent bug (inferred): if the Rust finalizer rejects a frame-count mismatch, recording_thread returns total_frames_per_camera = the number of videos rather than frames, with an empty info_json_path. Python then runs Path('').read_text() and crashes, so no Python-format files are written, though the native CSVs and videos remain. Evidence: upstream/sfn26:skellycam-rust/src/recording/finalizer.rs:98-106; upstream/sfn26:skellycam-rust/src/recording/recording_thread.rs:399,409-417; upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/camera_group/rust_camera_group.py:148; upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/camera_group/rust_recording.py:13.

Rust path encoder: an external ffmpeg (imageio_ffmpeg) runs libx264, preset ultrafast, CRF 18, yuv420p, in MP4. Dropping a VideoRecorder kills ffmpeg and leaves a partial MP4, so the container is still not crash-tolerant. Evidence: upstream/sfn26:skellycam-rust/src/recording/recorder.rs:37-47,141-153,265-276; upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/camera_group/rust_camera_group.py:282-285.

Rust audio sidecar: <name>.audio_timestamps.json now holds per-chunk ADC timestamps, PortAudio status flags and the dropped-chunk count. Stop fails if any chunk was dropped or any status error occurred. This partly addresses R11 for the Rust path only. Evidence: upstream/sfn26:skellycam-rust/src/recording/audio.rs:210-225.

Rust path: start reports success before the recorders exist. The ffmpeg spawn is deferred to the first multiframe, and spawn or CSV failures only log and end the recording thread, so any recorder failure, not just a reused name, shows up only at stop as 'Rust recorder did not produce video frames'. Evidence: upstream/sfn26:skellycam-rust/src/camera_group/dispatcher.rs:166-195; upstream/sfn26:skellycam-rust/src/recording/recording_thread.rs:206-267.

upstream/main and upstream/development-streaming: their extra commits change nothing in this group. development-streaming (169caf63, a92cae3e) only adds '# noqa: TC00x' comments to recording_finalizer.py, video_filename.py, sequential_video_reader.py, camera_group_manager.py and opencv_camera_loop.py. main's 3 commits (06771043, 26509b06, 524e5fc5) touch logging, pubsub closure and device detection only. Evidence: git diff upstream/sfn26...upstream/development-streaming -- skellycam/core/recorders/; git diff --stat upstream/sfn26...upstream/main.

The core claim holds: the file layout is the same and the info JSON gained three fields. The summary says the info JSON is "the one change", but three other output-affecting changes are on the same Python path in sfn26.
(1) The `_stats.json` contents changed. d091ecef (2026-08-08, "add checks for numpy objects when serializing timestamp stats", #141) is not an ancestor of 23ccbf20 but is in sfn26. It adds a branch for recarrays with named fields (upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/timestamps/recording_timestamp_stats.py:135-147). So the statistic blocks that the review measured as `{}` should now be filled in (inferred; not run).
(2) `save_to_file` can now fail and block the rest of finalize. It runs first in `finalize_recording` (upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/recorders/recording_finalizer.py:55; that file is unchanged). In sfn26 it calls `VideoAssociations.resolve_paths` (recording_info.py:86-90), which uses `resolve(strict=True)` and requires each camera's video to exist as a file (video_associations.py:37-43). It also raises if a config key disagrees with its `camera_id` (:83-85), and `video_file_path_from_camera_config` raises if more than one file matches the stem or the extension conflicts (:114-119). Any of these errors stops finalize before the timestamps, stats and README are written, and no info JSON is written either. At 23ccbf20 the path was only built, never checked. Effect is inferred: a camera whose video file is missing at stop now loses the whole finalize output, not just its video.
(3) `process_and_save_recording_timestamps` now raises if the cameras in the frame metadata differ from the cameras in the configs. It also reorders the metadata to config order (numpy_timestamps/process_and_save_recording_timestamps.py:32-36 and 84-87). In that case the result is now no CSVs or stats, instead of CSVs under the wrong camera names. The info JSON has already been written by then. This matters for R6 more than for the layout.

That only holds until the first config update that does not restart the stream, such as an exposure or rotation change at the same resolution and framerate.

How it breaks:
- Camera::configure overwrites the whole shared config with the requested config, including framerate (default -1.0). See upstream/sfn26:skellycam-rust/src/camera/camera.rs:84-87, called from camera_group.rs:395 and :676 whenever camera_config_eq finds a change (camera_group.rs:812-818; exposure is one of the compared fields).

- apply_config therefore sees old -1 and new -1, so needs_restart is false (camera_thread.rs:126-128) and there is no write-back of format_info.fps. Lines :267-268 then copy the -1 into active_config.framerate.
- At record time, dispatcher.rs:380-390 sees framerate <= 0 and uses 30.0.

Inferred effect:
- After any exposure tweak, every camera gets a 30.0 fps header whatever its negotiated rate. That is harmless for 30 fps cameras. A camera on a 60 fps format, when it actually runs at 60, gets a 30 fps header and plays at half speed. When the barrier holds it near 30, the fallback happens to come out about right. Before such a tweak, the summary's own concern applies instead: a 60 header on about 30 fps of real delivery.
- With an explicit framerate request that no format offers exactly (for example 60 on a 30-only camera), the same path leaves the requested 60 in the shared config. The header is then 60 while frames arrive at about 30.

So the header is "nominal negotiated fps, or the requested value, or 30.0 after a config update that does not restart the stream". It is never measured. The stamp-placement bias from the Python path is gone. R3 (different header rates within one group) is fixed only when the cameras end up with the same nominal or fallback value.

The worker monitor used to call os.kill(os.getpid(), SIGTERM) when the kill flag was set; it now calls signal.raise_signal(SIGTERM), which on Windows runs the installed Python handler (uvicorn's, or __main__.handle_signal) instead of TerminateProcess, so exit 15 should no longer happen (inferred, not run). (2) Rust is not the default backend: CameraBackendManager starts with backend="python", and Rust is used only when a caller passes backend="rust". close_native_camera_groups does nothing unless the backend is rust. (3) Caveat the summary missed: close_native_camera_groups is awaited before the kill flag is set, with no try/except. If a Rust finalize fails, RustCameraGroupManager raises an ExceptionGroup. The kill flag is then never set and the endpoint returns HTTP 500, so the server stays up instead of shutting down. Electron then reports 'Python was left running...' (inferred). That is fail-safe rather than a hard kill, but /shutdown does not shut down. (4) The 5 s Electron timeout point is right. The reply waits for close plus finalize, so a finalize longer than 5 s makes Electron throw while Python keeps going (inferred). (5) For contrast, upstream/main still has the old os.kill in both shutdown.py and worker_registry.py, but main has no Rust backend.

votes.correction: FIXED holds for the Rust path, with one caveat the summary leaves out. `/shutdown` awaits `close_native_camera_groups()` without a try/except before it sets the kill flag. If a Rust group fails to close or finalize, `RustCameraGroupManager.close_all_camera_groups` raises an ExceptionGroup. In that case `/shutdown` returns HTTP 500, the kill flag is never set, and the server keeps running; it is not killed. Electron then throws "Python was left running" and waits for the process to exit, which may never happen. This is a graceful failure to shut down, not a hard kill, so it does not reopen S2. The Rust backend is not the default: it must be chosen per camera group (the API defaults to python; the UI offers "Rust / OpenPNP").
votes.evidence:
The route I took was the git log and diffs of the shutdown-related files, then their call sites.
- Commits since 23ccbf20 that touch these files: `git log 23ccbf20..upstream/sfn26` lists d65707a1 ("Prioritize video finalization during camera and application shutdown") and 6cb170f2 (Rust backend) for shutdown.py, plus 43e2b968 for worker_registry/__main__/app.

How it was hard-killed at the base: 23ccbf20 shutdown.py called `os.kill(os.getpid(), signal.SIGTERM)`, and 23ccbf20 worker_registry.py:96,107 did the same. On Windows that terminates the process without running Python's handler or any cleanup.

What sfn26 does instead (one endpoint, used by both backends):
1. upstream/sfn26:skellycam/api/http/app/shutdown.py:37-45 awaits `close_native_camera_groups()`, sets `global_kill_flag`, then returns a 200 JSON reply. The `os`/`signal` imports are gone.
2. upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/ipc/process_management/worker_registry.py:106-113: the monitor thread (started at :68-73 from __main__.py:44) sees the flag, calls `wait_for_recording_save()` on its workers, then `signal.raise_signal(signal.SIGTERM)`. The comment at :110-111 says this replaces `os.kill` because of Windows. `raise_signal` runs the installed Python handler. During serve that is uvicorn's own handler (uvicorn 0.54.0 per uv.lock:1737); afterwards it is `handle_signal` at __main__.py:48-55, which sets `server.should_exit`.
3. The server then exits normally. The lifespan shutdown runs (app.py:61-71, which calls `close_native_camera_groups` a second time, harmlessly). The `finally` block in __main__.py:81-88 calls `worker_registry.shutdown_all()`. `os._exit(0)` (__main__.py:109) is reached only after `asyncio.run` returns.
4. upstream/sfn26:skellycam/tests/test_hardware_regressions.py:93-94 checks that `raise_signal` reaches the handler.

The Rust-specific part:
- upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/camera_group/camera_group_manager.py:268-271 closes groups only when `backend == "rust"`. The call chain is `CameraBackendManager.close_all_camera_groups` (camera_backend_manager.py:70-73, under `_configuration_lock`) → `RustCameraGroupManager.close_all_camera_groups` (rust_camera_group.py:340-354) → `RustCameraGroup.close` (rust_camera_group.py:78-86). That calls `stop_recording` if a recording is active: `stop_group_recording`, then the audio recorder stops, then `finalize_native_recording` (rust_camera_group.py:137-155), then `close_group`. So an active Rust recording is stopped and finalized before the reply, as claimed.
- The caveat comes from rust_camera_group.py:353-354, which raises an ExceptionGroup if any group close fails. Because shutdown.py:37 has no try/except, line 38 never runs, so the kill flag stays unset.

Backend selection:
- skellycam/api/http/cameras/camera_router.py:25 has `backend: CameraBackend = "python"`.
- camera_backend_manager.py:26 initialises `self.backend = "python"`; :35-41 switches the backend per create request.
- The UI option is in skellycam-ui/src/components/camera-config-tree-view/CameraConfigSidebarPanel.tsx:69.

Electron:
- upstream/sfn26:skellycam-ui/electron/main/services/graceful-python-shutdown.ts:16-22 uses `AbortSignal.timeout(5000)`. On a timeout or a non-OK reply it throws "Python was left running..." and does not kill the process tree.
- So a Rust finalize longer than 5 s makes Electron report failure while Python keeps finalizing and then exits on its own. That matches the summary's inferred point.

Other branches: upstream/main has no Rust files at all. Its `git diff upstream/sfn26 upstream/main` removes rust_camera_group.py and camera_backend_manager.py, so this Rust-path verdict applies to sfn26 only.

A single input-overflow flag in a long take would leave the native MP4s/CSVs without SkellyCam's finalized timestamps/info outputs, and stop_recording_all_groups raises an ExceptionGroup (lines 371-379). Rust path: the ADC timestamp depends on the host API filling time_info.inputBufferAdcTime and currentTime in the same timebase. If a host API (e.g. some MME/WDM-KS configurations) leaves inputBufferAdcTime at 0, chunk_adc_timestamps_perf_ns would be offset by -currentTime and be meaningless. No check or fallback exists (audio.rs:92). Low confidence; this depends on the PortAudio host API.

Rust path sidecar semantics differ from Python. duration_seconds is sample-count based (total_frames/RATE), where Python uses last-chunk host time minus the start stamp. end_perf_counter_ns is the host time of the last chunk. There are new keys (chunk_adc_timestamps_perf_ns, chunk_sample_counts, portaudio_status_flags, dropped_chunks, stream_error), and mean/std_chunk_duration_seconds are dropped. Rust path: the audio stream is started via the Rust thread but uses sounddevice's private attribute `_libname` to locate the PortAudio DLL (rust_camera_group.py:122). A sounddevice upgrade that renames it would break microphone recording on the Rust backend only.

The standalone Rust HTTP server (skellycam-rust/src/api/camera_routes.rs:305-345) accepts mic_device_index but only logs it. It never starts audio, so microphone recording exists only when Rust is embedded via the Python RustCameraGroup adapter.

Python path close() now stops audio via asyncio.to_thread (upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/camera_group/camera_group.py:333), but stop_recording still calls self._audio_recorder.stop() synchronously on the event loop (line 288), including the WAV write of the whole in-RAM buffer. upstream/main and upstream/development-streaming extra commits (not in sfn26) contain no audio/microphone changes (diff upstream/sfn26...<ref> has 0 audio/microphone matches), so they are omitted.

# Rust recording path on upstream/sfn26 (765bf82d): overview

All of this comes from reading the code. Nothing was built or run, and anything marked **inferred** is a prediction. The Rust backend exists only on sfn26: `upstream/main` and `upstream/development-streaming` have no `skellycam-rust/` directory, and none of their extra commits touch this path. The Rust recording code arrived in `6cb170f2` ("Add selectable Rust camera capture with native audio and bundled runtimes"). Two later commits also touched the Rust recording files: `43e2b968` and `f1aefa95`.

## 1. Default backend, how it is chosen, and whether it ships

- **Python/OpenCV is the default on every OS.** No code picks a backend by OS.
  - `upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/camera_group/camera_backend_manager.py:26` sets `self.backend = "python"`, and `:30` defaults the parameter to `backend="python"`.
  - `:39` swaps in `RustCameraGroupManager` only when the request asks for `"rust"`.
- **It is chosen per request, through the API body.** `CameraGroupCreateRequest.backend: CameraBackend = "python"` is at `upstream/sfn26:skellycam/api/http/cameras/camera_router.py:25`, and it is passed on at `:127`.
- **The UI has a dropdown.** "Python / OpenCV" or "Rust / OpenPNP" (`skellycam-ui/src/components/camera-config-tree-view/CameraConfigSidebarPanel.tsx:58-70`). It defaults to `'python'` (`skellycam-ui/src/store/slices/cameras/cameras-slice.ts:31`) and is locked while cameras are connected (`:42-45`; `camera_backend_manager.py:35-37`).
- **There is no environment variable or config field.** The `USE_RUST_BACKEND: bool = True` flag described at `upstream/sfn26:skellycam-rust/README.md:134-139` is stale: `git grep USE_RUST_BACKEND` finds it only in that README. The developer notes agree that Python is the default: `RUST-BACKEND-DEVELOPMENT.md:3-6`.
- **It ships, and it is a required dependency.**
  - `pyproject.toml:76` lists `"skellycam-rust", # Required native backend`, built from source with `skellycam-rust = { path = "skellycam-rust" }` (`:82`).
  - `imageio-ffmpeg` (`:77`) supplies the encoder.
  - Every `uv sync` compiles the crate, even when the Python backend is used (`RUST-BACKEND-DEVELOPMENT.md:10-11`).
  - The PyInstaller spec bundles `_skellycam_rust`, `imageio_ffmpeg` and PortAudio (`skellycam.spec:9-18`).
  - The installer workflow builds Rust on all 5 platform/arch targets (`.github/workflows/build-installers-pyinstaller.yml:180-187`).
- **Only Windows x64 has been checked, and only that it builds and imports.**
  - `RUST-BACKEND-DEVELOPMENT.md:34-38` and `:96-98` record that local validation covers Windows x64.
  - On macOS ARM64 and Linux x64 it built and imported with no cameras attached (`:100-114`).
  - `skellycam-rust/README.md:189-191` says "Mac and Linux are not currently tested".

## 2. Capture API per OS

- **Library:** openpnp-capture, called through FFI from one thread per camera. Prebuilt static libraries come from the `jonmatthis/openpnp-capture` fork (`skellycam-rust/build.rs:1-14`, `:55-63`).
- **Windows:** DirectShow (`skellycam-rust/src/camera/camera_thread.rs:1`; `README.md:38`).
- **macOS:** AVFoundation, according to the README (`README.md:194`). Untested.
- **Linux:** V4L2, according to the README (`README.md:194`). Untested.
- **Only MJPEG formats are accepted.** Format selection filters on `info.fourcc == FOURCC_MJPG` (`camera_thread.rs:519`, `:538`, `:567`, `:595`, `:623`).
- **The only OS-specific code** in the crate is one `#[cfg(target_os = "windows")]` at `skellycam-rust/src/camera_group/jpeg_transform.rs:50`.

## 3. Files a Rust-backend recording writes

**The Rust side writes these** (`skellycam-rust/src/camera_group/dispatcher.rs:354-374`):

```
<recording_directory>/<recording_name>/
├── native_recording_summary.json                       finalizer.rs:119 (at stop)
└── synchronized_videos/
    ├── <name>.id-<cam_id>.idx-<cam_index>.mp4          dispatcher.rs:373 (during)
    └── timestamps/camera_timestamps/
        └── <name>.camera<cam_id>.native_timestamps.csv dispatcher.rs:374 (during)
```

Python passes `recording_name` as the label, so the session folder matches Python's `full_recording_path` (`rust_camera_group.py:126-129`; `recording_info.py:42`).

**Python then adds everything the review listed in §2.** `RustCameraGroup.stop_recording` calls `finalize_native_recording` (`skellycam/core/camera_group/rust_recording.py:12-55`), which runs the same `RecordingFinalizer` as the Python path:

- the info JSON (`recording_finalizer.py:55`);
- the Python per-camera CSV `<name>.camera<id>.timestamps.csv`, the multiframe CSV and the stats (`:57-61`; path at `recording_timing_reader.py:15`);
- the README (`:64`);
- `validate_recording` (`:65`).

The VFR/audio remux is **still commented out** (`:63`).

**Video encoding** (`skellycam-rust/src/recording/recorder.rs`):

- **The camera's MJPEG is decoded and re-encoded.** Each camera has an ffmpeg subprocess fed raw JPEG bytes on stdin (`recorder.rs:1-6`, `:197-209`). The ffmpeg binary is the imageio-ffmpeg executable (`rust_camera_group.py:285`).
- **Command** (`:141-153`): `-y -f image2pipe -c:v mjpeg -s WxH -r <fps> -i pipe:0 -c:v libx264 -preset ultrafast -crf 18 -pix_fmt yuv420p -an <out>.mp4`.
- **Settings** (defaults at `:37-47`; always `VideoRecorderConfig::default()`, `dispatcher.rs:403`): libx264, preset ultrafast, CRF 18, yuv420p, MP4 container.
- **Not set:** bitrate, GOP, B-frames or `movflags`.
  - **Inferred:** x264 defaults plus ultrafast give keyint 250 with scenecut off, so an I-frame every 250 frames, no B-frames, CAVLC, probably signalled Constrained Baseline.
  - **Inferred:** CRF rate control means file size depends on content and quality, not on the header rate. That replaces the review's R4 (fixed 1 bit/pixel MSMF/NVENC bitrate) for this path.
- **Frame rate is constant, at the camera mode's nominal rate.**
  - `-r target_fps` on the input gives a CFR file with no per-frame timestamps.
  - `target_fps` is the negotiated openpnp format rate (`dispatcher.rs:380-390`), written by the camera thread as `guard.framerate = format_info.fps` (`camera_thread.rs:167`, `:219`). `fps` is a `u32` (`camera/ffi.rs:20`). The fallback when it is missing is 30.0.
  - **Inferred effect on R3:** the pre-recording median estimate that caused the +9–11% header bias is gone. The header will read, for example, exactly 30 for a 30 fps mode, and all cameras in one mode get the same value. Durations will be correct only if the camera really delivers its nominal rate. Dropped or slow frames are still hidden by the CFR file.
- **Rotation is applied before recording, without re-encoding the JPEG.** The dispatcher rotates in the DCT domain (`dispatcher.rs:197-214`; `jpeg_transform.rs:1-5`).
- **The Rust side does no shape check of its own,** but Python's `validate_recording` still checks shape and frame count (`recording_finalizer.py:126-208`).

## 4. When timestamps and CSVs are written, and their format

- **The native CSV is written incrementally, flushed after every row.** It is created with its header at recorder setup, and each frame appends a row and calls `flush()` (`skellycam-rust/src/timestamps/csv_writer.rs:22-41`, `:53-72`). The call site is `recording_thread.rs:301-306`.
  - **Inferred:** `flush()` hands the data to the OS but does not fsync, so rows survive a process crash but not a power loss.
- **Native CSV columns (8):** `frame_number`, `timestamps.loop_start_ns`, `.frame_available_ns`, `.post_jpeg_extract_ns`, `.pre_send_ns`, `.gatherer_received_ns`, `.pre_frame_record_ns`, `.post_frame_record_ns` (`csv_writer.rs:28-37`).
- **Clock:** the Rust monotonic clock shifted once to Python's `perf_counter_ns` when the module is imported (`timestamps/performance.rs:31-33`, `:66`; `pyo3_bridge/mod.rs:29-35`, which also exposes the uncertainty as `clock_alignment_uncertainty_ns`).
  - `frame_available_ns` is stamped when `Cap_hasNewFrame` turns true (`camera_thread.rs:351`, `:367-370`).
  - `loop_start_ns` is stamped just after the barrier, at the start of the wait (`:474-479`).
- **The Python 27-column CSV, the multiframe CSV and the stats are written only at stop**, from the native CSV. `rust_recording.py:32-44` maps the columns:
  - `pre_frame_grab_ns` ← `loop_start_ns`
  - `post_frame_grab_ns` ← `frame_available_ns`
  - retrieve ← `post_jpeg_extract_ns`
  - shm copy ← `pre_send_ns` / `gatherer_received_ns`
- **Inferred:** the Python CSV's main timestamp is still the grab midpoint (`create_camera_csvs.py:49-51`). For Rust that is the midpoint of loop start and frame-available, so it sits up to half the wait time before the frame actually arrived. `frame_available_ns`, available only in the native CSV, is the more meaningful stamp.
- **Rust also computes recording stats** and returns them as `stats_json` (`py_camera_group_manager.rs:542-545`), but `RustCameraGroup.stop_recording` never reads them (`rust_camera_group.py:143-155`).

## 5. Overlay

- **None.** The recorder receives the camera's own JPEG bytes, rotated only (`dispatcher.rs:216-221`, `:306-319`).
- `git grep -iE "overlay|annotat|putText|draw_text"` over `skellycam-rust/src` finds nothing.
- **R2 (overlay burned into the recording) does not apply to this path.** The Python/OpenCV path is reviewed separately.

## 6. Audio

- **Capture:** PortAudio, called from Rust through the PortAudio library sounddevice already loaded (`skellycam-rust/src/recording/audio.rs:1-3`, `:50-63`; `rust_camera_group.py:119-125`).
  - Format: 44.1 kHz, 1024-frame blocks, int16, up to 2 channels (`audio.rs:16-17`, `:159-162`).
  - Data passes through a lock-free ring buffer and is written to the WAV as it arrives through hound/BufWriter (`:152`, `:166-169`, `:190-191`), so audio no longer piles up in RAM.
- **Timing:**
  - `start_perf_counter_ns` is now taken after `Pa_OpenStream` and just before `Pa_StartStream` (`:170-174`), so device-open time is no longer included.
  - Each chunk carries both the callback host time and an ADC time, computed as host time + (`inputBufferAdcTime` − `currentTime`) (`:89-92`).
  - The sidecar records dropped chunks and status flags (`:210-219`).
  - The sidecar `<name>.audio_timestamps.json` is written only at stop (`:220-222`).
- **Alignment and muxing: none.**
  - Audio starts before the video recorder is asked to start (`rust_camera_group.py:118-129`).
  - It stops after the video stops (`:142-147`, the `finally`).
  - The remux that would join them is commented out (`recording_finalizer.py:63`).
  - The WAV stays separate. A consumer must line up the sidecar stamps with the CSVs, as in R11, but with better stamps to work from.

## 7. Crash and kill behaviour

| Event | What survives |
| --- | --- |
| Clean stop, graceful `/shutdown`, or app lifespan exit | Everything. `close_native_camera_groups()` stops and fully finalizes Rust recordings before the kill flag is set (`api/http/app/shutdown.py:37`; `app.py:64`; `camera_group_manager.py:268-271`). This is better than the Python path, where a kill-flag shutdown writes no CSVs. |
| Server process hard-killed | The native CSVs, up to the last flushed row. ffmpeg is a separate child process: **inferred**, if it outlives the parent, stdin EOF lets it write a playable MP4; if the process tree is killed, the MP4 has no moov atom and is unreadable. Missing: the WAV header sizes (hound writes them only at `finalize`, `audio.rs:207`), the audio sidecar, `native_recording_summary.json`, and all the Python finalize outputs. |
| Recorder dropped without `finish()` (setup failure, recording thread exits on channel disconnect) | `Drop` kills ffmpeg, leaving a partial MP4 (`recorder.rs:86-87`, `:265-276`; `recording_thread.rs:335-340`). **Inferred:** if the gatherer disconnects mid-recording (`dispatcher.rs:327-329`), the handle is dropped this way. |
| Dispatcher `Shutdown` while recording | `handle.shutdown()` runs `finalize_all`, so the videos and native files are finalized (`dispatcher.rs:144-151`; `recording_thread.rs:326-332`). The Python finalize does not run on this path. |
| Microphone reports any dropped chunk or nonzero status flag | `AudioRecorder` raises at stop (`audio.rs:223-224`). That exception comes out of the `finally` at `rust_camera_group.py:145-147`, so `finalize_native_recording` (`:150-154`) never runs: no info JSON and no Python CSVs. **Inferred:** `CameraBackendManager._recording_requested` then stays `True` (`camera_backend_manager.py:86-92`), so later starts are refused until the cameras are closed. |

## 8. Unfinished, TODO or disabled

- **Encoder settings are hard-coded.** "In the future these will be user-configurable" (`recorder.rs:17-20`). There is no GOP, bitrate or `movflags` setting.
- **The remux is still disabled** (`recording_finalizer.py:63`), so there is no VFR file and no audio in the video.
- **The README's selection flag `USE_RUST_BACKEND` is stale** (`skellycam-rust/README.md:134-139`).
- **macOS and Linux capture and recording are untested** (`README.md:189-197`; `RUST-BACKEND-DEVELOPMENT.md:96-114`). The code comments assume DirectShow throughout (`camera_thread.rs:1`, `:372-374`; `ffi.rs:3`).
- **Known lifecycle race conditions** around hot-plugging and fast start/stop (`README.md:187`).
- **Polars is commented out of the build**, labelled "Phase 3 — recording" (`Cargo.toml:85-86`).
- **The Rust stats summary is computed but not used** (§4).
- **The recording thread's queue is unbounded** (`recording_thread.rs:5`, `:96-101`). **Inferred:** if ffmpeg falls behind, memory grows and the stop waits until the queue drains.
- **The Python finalize still runs synchronously on the event loop** (`rust_camera_group.py:150-154` → `RecordingFinalizer`), so R10 (finalize freezes the UI) applies to this path too (**inferred**).

# Completeness critique: REPORT.md findings vs upstream/sfn26 (765bf82d), main and development-streaming

Everything here comes from static reading with `git show` and `git grep`; nothing was built or run. "Inferred" marks a prediction. Python is still the default backend on sfn26 (`upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/camera_group/camera_backend_manager.py:26,30`), so every "python" verdict describes what users get by default.

## (a) Findings that were not checked, now checked on sfn26

**A1. §1 bullet 1: each camera process encodes synchronously inside the capture loop**
- **python: UNCHANGED.** `handle_video_recording` is still called inline in the loop (`upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/camera/opencv/opencv_camera_loop.py:106-112`), so a slow write still holds up every camera in lockstep.
- **rust: CHANGED.** Encoding runs in a recording thread and one ffmpeg child process per camera. The dispatcher only queues frames:
  - `upstream/sfn26:skellycam-rust/src/camera_group/dispatcher.rs:298-321`
  - `upstream/sfn26:skellycam-rust/src/recording/recording_thread.rs:96-101,280-314`
- Capture is no longer blocked by encoding, but see C1 in (c): a blocked ffmpeg can now hang the whole recording.

**A2. §4, codec choice per platform** (Linux falls back to `X264_PYAV`, macOS probably gets `avc1`, Windows tries FFmpeg/OpenH264 before MSMF)
- **python: UNCHANGED.** No diff to `fourcc_codec_helpers.py` (`git diff --stat 23ccbf20 upstream/sfn26 -- skellycam/core/recorders/videos/fourcc_codec_helpers.py` is empty). OpenCV is still pinned to 4.12.0.88, so whether OpenH264 is used still depends only on whether its DLL is present.
- **rust: NOT_APPLICABLE.** libx264 is used on every OS. macOS and Linux capture and recording are untested (`upstream/sfn26:skellycam-rust/README.md:189-197`).

**A3. §4a, FreeMoCap calibration recordings.** Checked against the local FreeMoCap checkout (development @ 5632778a, 2026-10-08).
- **Start and stop: still work (code).**
  - FreeMoCap calls `get_or_create_camera_group_manager(...).start_recording_all_groups(recording_info=...)` and `stop_recording_all_groups()`, then reads `[0][0]` (`freemocap/app/freemocap_application.py:63,74-87`).
  - On sfn26 that accessor returns a `CameraBackendManager` (`upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/camera_group/camera_group_manager.py:274-285`). It accepts the same keyword arguments and still returns a list of `(RecordingInfo, stats)` (`camera_backend_manager.py:75-92`).

- **Calibration solve: broken on sfn26 with this FreeMoCap (inferred).** The solve that `/freemocap/calibration/recording/stop` starts runs FreeMoCap nodes, which call `WorkerRegistry.create_worker` without the arguments it now requires (S3 evidence: `upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/ipc/process_management/worker_registry.py:133-143`). The recording would be written, but the solve would fail with a TypeError.
- **rust: recording works; realtime pipeline does not.**
  - The recording is clean (no overlay) and has an extra `*.native_timestamps.csv` in `camera_timestamps/`.
  - FreeMoCap's own fps helper globs `synchronized_videos/timestamps/**/*timestamps.csv` and takes the first match after sorting (`freemocap/core/tasks/mocap/mocap_helpers/recording_framerate.py:29-32,44-49`). It looks for the stats JSON first, though, and that is no longer empty (L3).

FreeMoCap's `create_or_update_camera_group(camera_configs=...)` also sends no backend, so it defaults to "python", and with a Rust group open it gets `CameraBackendInUseError` (`camera_backend_manager.py:35-37`).

The fixed serializer writes exactly that key, because it strips `_value` from the field names (`upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/timestamps/recording_timestamp_stats.py:135-142`). So FreeMoCap will now take its filter rate from the stats JSON rather than its CSV fallback.

**A9. §6 row: 30 failed grabs → repeated frame number → `_validate_frame_number` raises**
- **python: CHANGED.** After `MAX_FAIL_COUNT` failures the loop now raises `RuntimeError("…failed to capture a frame after N attempts")` (`upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/camera/opencv/opencv_camera_loop.py:86-92`; 87eddca2). It also fires when not recording.
- **rust: CHANGED, and worse for the video files (inferred).** Any capture error on one camera destroys every camera's video for the take:
  1. The camera thread exits on any of: a frame wait longer than 5 s (`upstream/sfn26:skellycam-rust/src/camera/camera_thread.rs:355-364`), a `getFrameSize` or `captureFrameRaw` failure (`:377-418`), or a frame-number mismatch, which makes the gatherer panic (`upstream/sfn26:skellycam-rust/src/camera_group/gatherer.rs:324-330`).

  3. The dispatcher sees `Disconnected` and exits without Stop (`dispatcher.rs:327-330`).
  4. The recording thread exits on the dropped channel (`recording_thread.rs:335-340`).
  5. `VideoRecorder::drop` kills ffmpeg (`recorder.rs:265-276`), which leaves MP4s with no moov atom. Only the native CSVs survive.
  6. The Python stop then fails with "Dispatcher disconnected" (`upstream/sfn26:skellycam-rust/src/camera_group/camera_group.rs:600-611`). `_recording_requested` stays True.

**A10. §8: `video_frame_metadata` is never cleared**
- **python: UNCHANGED** (`upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/recorders/videos/video_recorder.py:33,115-118`). Still harmless, because each recording gets a new recorder.
- **rust: NOT_APPLICABLE.** The Rust recorder `mem::take`s its timestamps (`recorder.rs:253`).

**A11. §8: `finish_recording` returns `None` and one caller ignores it**
- **python: UNCHANGED** (`upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/camera/opencv/opencv_helpers/handle_recording_updates.py:35,59-68`). Still harmless: line 40 now sets `video_recorder = None` explicitly.

**A12. §4, GOP consequences for random access** (how skellycam's own playback seeks)
- **python: UNCHANGED.** The encoder is unchanged. Playback now serves the file as-is to the browser (`upstream/sfn26:skellycam/api/http/playback/playback_router.py:237-277`), and `sequential_video_reader.py` is used by no production code (only tests).
- **rust: CHANGED (inferred).** With keyint 250 and scenecut off, random access means decoding up to 249 frames.

## (b) Disagreements and inconsistencies, resolved

**B1. R7 [sfn26/rust]: votes CONFIRMED (FIXED) vs REFUTED→PARTLY_FIXED. Resolution: FIXED for skellycam as shipped; a separate hazard remains only in the standalone Rust binary.**
- Through Python, a second start is refused twice:
  - `CameraBackendManager.start_recording_all_groups` returns 409 (`upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/camera_group/camera_backend_manager.py:75-84`).
  - `RustCameraGroup.start_recording` raises if already recording (`rust_camera_group.py:115-116`).
- Stop is a synchronous request/response (`camera_group.rs:600-611`), so there is no queue of stale finished-messages. The R7 symptom (finalizing the previous recording) cannot happen.
- The dispatcher itself has no guard. A second `StartRecording` overwrites `pending_recording` (`dispatcher.rs:96-102`), and the next multiframe replaces `recording_handle` (`:177-182`). The old thread then sees the disconnect and ffmpeg is killed: the old take is destroyed, not mis-finalized.
- That path is reachable only from the standalone `skellycam-rust` binary's start route (`upstream/sfn26:skellycam-rust/Cargo.toml` `[[bin]]`; `skellycam-rust/src/api/camera_routes.rs:305`). The PyInstaller build bundles only `_skellycam_rust`.
- So the dispatcher hazard is a different failure in an unshipped binary. It does not mean R7 is only partly fixed.

**B2. C3/F-new [rust] "GOP = keyint 250 plus scenecut" vs Rust overview "scenecut off". Resolution: the overview is right.**
- `recorder.rs:43-44` (preset `ultrafast`) and `:141-153` set no `-g` and no x264 parameters.
- x264's ultrafast preset sets scenecut 0, bframes 0, no CABAC, no 8x8dct, weightp 0 and no deblocking (x264 source `common/base.c`, preset apply, which is outside the repo).
- So the GOP is a fixed I-frame every 250 frames with no scene-cut I-frames, signalled Constrained Baseline (inferred, not probed).

**B3. S1 [python] "validate check-1 weakness carries over" vs files-layout new observation "missing video aborts finalize at save_to_file". Resolution: both readings are accurate, and the second one decides the outcome.**
- The check-1 code is byte-for-byte the same (`upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/recorders/recording_finalizer.py:138-145`).
- It can no longer see a missing file, though: `save_to_file`'s strict `resolve_paths` raises first (`recording_info.py:86-90`; `video_associations.py:41`). See A7.
- Verdict for the §8 item: PARTLY_FIXED. A missing video is now a loud error, but it costs every finalize output.

**B4. Rust ffmpeg stderr "possible stall, not verified" (codec group). Resolution: likely real, and worse than a stall: a deadlock at stop (inferred, now supported by the library source).**
- ffmpeg-sidecar 2.5.1 (`upstream/sfn26:skellycam-rust/Cargo.lock:762-763`):
  - `new_with_path` pipes stdin, stdout and stderr, and adds `-loglevel level+info`.
  - `FfmpegChild::wait()` copies stderr to a sink only when it is called, with the comment "we need to run it to completion to avoid a deadlock".
  - Source: docs.rs `ffmpeg-sidecar/2.5.1/src/command.rs` and `child.rs`, fetched read-only.
- skellycam-rust reads stderr nowhere except `finish()` → `wait()` (`recorder.rs:233-240`; `git grep stderr` finds only that comment).
- At info level, ffmpeg prints a progress line about every 0.5 s. Once the stderr pipe fills, ffmpeg blocks; that is roughly 4 KB on Windows anonymous pipes (about 10–30 s) and 64 KB on Linux and macOS (a few minutes). Then this chain follows:
  1. ffmpeg stops reading stdin.
  2. `feed_frame`'s `write_all` blocks (`recorder.rs:206-209`).
  3. The recording thread is stuck inside `FeedFrames`, so the queued `Stop` is never processed (`recording_thread.rs:280-324`).
  4. `HandleRecording::stop` waits on `rx.recv()` with no timeout (`:108-127`).
  5. Python's `to_thread(stop_group_recording)` never returns.
  6. `close()` hangs too, because it calls `stop_recording` first (`rust_camera_group.py:81-85`).
  7. Meanwhile the unbounded channel takes on every JPEG.
- The only Rust recording test records 150 frames, about 5 s (`upstream/sfn26:skellycam-rust/src/tests/recording_tests.rs:20-22`), which is too short to show this.
- Severity is high if true. It needs one Rust recording longer than 60 s on Windows to confirm.

**B5. L7 [rust] "info JSON framerate is the requested value, e.g. −1" vs F1 [rust] "the header uses the negotiated fps from `shared_config`". Not a conflict.**
- `shared_config` is Rust-internal (`camera_thread.rs:167,219`; `dispatcher.rs:380-390`).
- The Python `self._configs` is the requested set (`rust_camera_group.py:108`).
- Both claims hold: the negotiated rate is recorded nowhere except the ffmpeg `-r`.

**B6. R8 [python] FIXED vs lifecycle new observation "a hung camera blocks close forever". Resolution: FIXED for the reported trigger (a dead process), with a new caveat.**
- `wait_for_recording_save` has no timeout for a process that is alive but hung (`upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/ipc/process_management/managed_worker.py:66-74`).
- Keep FIXED, and list the hung-process case as a new item.

No other votes disagreed. The C4 rust and R1 rust predictions about a hard kill agree; they are inferred and assume ffmpeg ignores SIGPIPE on POSIX.

## (c) Recording-relevant sfn26 changes nobody reported

**C1. The Rust stderr deadlock** in B4 was listed only as "possible". It should be promoted to a headline Rust risk.

**C2. On Rust, a capture error on any single camera destroys every camera's video for the take** (A9). This is a new failure mode with no Python equivalent; Python keeps playable videos.

**C3. Recorder creation moved after config application in each loop iteration.**
- **What changed:** in `camera_loop_update_checks`, `check_for_new_recording_info` now runs after `check_for_new_config` (`upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/camera/opencv/opencv_helpers/camera_loop_update_checks.py:30-48`; d65707a1).
- **Effect (inferred):** if a config update and a recording start land in the same iteration, the writer now opens with the new config.
- Recorder creation is also wrapped so a failure closes the writer and clears `recording_in_progress` (`handle_recording_updates.py:39-56`).

**C4. Regression: fallback-codec videos are no longer playable in skellycam's playback view (inferred).**
- `transcode_to_h264.py` was deleted (59a3e7b1), and `stream_video` now returns the raw file for `.avi` (`video/x-msvideo`) too (`upstream/sfn26:skellycam/api/http/playback/playback_router.py:260-277`).
- `browser_stream.py` would solve this but has no production caller.
- Recordings made with the `mp4v`, XVID or MJPG fallbacks (§4's last-resort row) will not play in Chromium.
- L5 marked the sidecar FIXED without noting that the problem it handled is now unhandled.

**C5. An exposure sweep can land inside a recording (inferred).**
- `CameraBackendManager._create_or_update` runs `recommend_exposure` whenever a RECOMMEND config is applied (`upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/camera_group/camera_backend_manager.py:42-56`).
- It does not check `_recording_requested`, and in-place updates are allowed while recording on both backends (`camera_group_manager.py:101-114`; `rust_camera_group.py:90-110`).
- The sweep steps through exposures −12…−5 for at least 10 frames each (`upstream/sfn26:skellycam/core/camera_group/tasks/recommend_exposure.py:19-75`). If it runs during a recording, those roughly 80+ frames of changing brightness go into the take.
- The UI blocks apply while recording; non-UI clients are not blocked.

**C6. Rust frame-rate stats are computed but thrown away.**
- The dispatcher measures `camera_fps` from `frame_available_ns` (`dispatcher.rs:242-262`) and the finalizer gets a `RecordingStatsSummary`.
- `native_recording_summary.json` has no stats field, and Python never reads `stats_json` (`rust_camera_group.py:143-155`). The measured rate never reaches disk except through the Python CSV pipeline.
- This partly overlaps L3 rust, but nobody noted that the fps measurement exists.

**C7. Dead code next to the recorder.** `video_copy_plan.py`, `video_derivation.py`, `sequential_video_reader.py`, `browser_stream.py` and `PyavVideoWriter.set_container_metadata` have no production caller (`git grep` finds only tests). They change no behaviour, but readers should not take them as active recording features.

**C8. `ms_to_ns` now returns rounded int64 and rejects NaN and overflow** (`upstream/sfn26:skellycam/utilities/time_unit_conversion.py:11-38`; f1aefa95). No production caller was found, so recordings are unaffected.

**C9. The sfn26 Rust path has no recording guard on `apply()` and routes frames to files by position** (R6 rust). This was reported, but it adds to C2 and A8: a non-UI client changing cameras, rotation or exposure mid-recording on Rust has three separate ways to corrupt the take.

**main and development-streaming deltas:** nothing further. Their 5 extra commits touch none of the items above.
